newsitem.title: USA: U.S. must reduce Chinese trade barriers - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. must reduce Chinese trade barriers - Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Wednesday that more work was needed to reduce Chinese trade barriers but that U.S. firms needed to focus on developing the Chinese market.
"There are trade impediments in China and I think that we need to continue to work with China on reducing those impediments," Rubin told CNN's Moneyline program.
"At the same time ... our private sector has to focus on energetically investing itself, developing its own markets in China," he added.
Asked if he was worried by the level of the trade deficit with China, Rubin said, "It's a very complicated question."
A "fair" proportion of that deficit was due to the transfer of low wage production from other Asian countries, he said.
Commenting on the overall U.S. trade deficit, Rubin said that the current strength of the U.S. economy compared with other countries was tending to increase the deficit.
"But, over time, I think the competitiveness of our industry and the focus we've had on bringing trade barriers down should lead to lower trade deficits," he said.
The Commerce Department reported earlier on Wednesday that record overseas sales helped shrink the U.S. trade deficit to $8.51 billion in March, down almost 20 percent from February.
There was also a sharp improvement in the monthly deficit with China, which fell 22.4 percent to $2.59 billion in March.
